message.content: {"caption":"Three schematic ways to update reasoning memory: mapping individual memories to trajectories, contrasting parallel trajectories, and refining a trajectory sequentially.","description":"A three-panel diagram. (a) “Vanilla TTS (MaTTS w/o aggregation)” shows rows for Mem 1, Mem 2, …, Mem n. Each memory item points right to a corresponding gray trajectory box (Traj 1, Traj 2, …, Traj n), which points right to a notebook/lightbulb icon labeled New Mem 1, New Mem 2, …, New Mem n. A bottom timeline runs rightward from Task q_i to Task q_{i+1}. (b) “MaTTS - Parallel” shows a Current memory notebook and agent icon branching via arrows to a dashed box containing Trajectory 1, Trajectory 2, and Trajectory n. Trajectory 1 and Trajectory n have green check marks; Trajectory 2 has a red cross. The trajectories feed a small comparison graphic labeled “Self-Contrast,” followed by a blue right-pointing arrow to a New memory notebook and agent icon. The bottom timeline runs from Task q_i to Task q_{i+1}. (c) “MaTTS - Sequential” shows a Current memory notebook and agent icon pointing to a dashed “Self-Refine” box. Inside, gray refinement/editing symbols with red marks and curved red arrows appear above the trajectory labels Traj, Traj′, and an ellipsis, indicating successive refinement steps. A blue right-pointing arrow leads from the box to a New memory notebook and agent icon. Its bottom timeline also runs from Task q_i to Task q_{i+1}.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
